nodes.label: Legacy Bridge
nodes.rationale: It temporarily connects legacy services and queues to the core runtime, but must disappear as domains migrate.

nodes.label: Per-Module Schema Ownership
nodes.rationale: Modules share PostgreSQL but own their tables and migrations; peers do not import each other's schemas.

nodes.label: Module-Owned Public Types
nodes.rationale: The shared types package is kept small and framework-only to avoid a central type bottleneck.

nodes.label: Vertical-Slice Modules
nodes.rationale: A module owns schema, services, routes, events, jobs, and UI so a domain change remains localized.

nodes.label: Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: The roadmap moves business domains into independently owned vertical-slice modules while retaining one deployable application.

nodes.label: Vertical-Slice Module
nodes.rationale: A credible slice includes backend routes, domain service, schema ownership, permissions, frontend integration, and tests.

nodes.label: pnpm Workspace Topology
nodes.rationale: The workspace includes apps, packages, and modules, aligning the repository layout with the modular-monolith architecture.

nodes.label: Cross-Module Foreign Key Reference Map
nodes.rationale: Tenant, user, client, subscription, and component relationships cross module boundaries; modules use type-only imports and resolve behavior through services at runtime.

nodes.label: Per-Module Database Schema Ownership
nodes.rationale: Schema files should move into their owning modules, while core tables remain in the API and cross-module interactions use runtime service calls.

nodes.label: Canonical Permission Convention
nodes.rationale: Permissions are named {module}.{resource}.{action}, declared by modules, seeded after boot, and cached roles are invalidated after seeding.

nodes.label: Single Database Connection
nodes.rationale: The application uses one connection pool; the schema index is only a re-export barrel.

nodes.label: Persistent Event Bus
nodes.rationale: Events are persisted before asynchronous dispatch, enabling recovery and replay after a crash.

nodes.label: Microservice Extraction Path
nodes.rationale: Service interfaces and events preserve boundaries while remaining in-process until independent scaling or ownership warrants a split.

nodes.label: Single-Tenant-First Scope
nodes.rationale: Retain tenant identifiers but defer SaaS-grade isolation and tenant-switching UI while validating the self-hosted product.

nodes.label: Verified Money-Core Rebuild
nodes.rationale: The product focus is a trustworthy end-to-end money path before feature breadth, differentiated by cent-exact Stripe reconciliation.

nodes.label: Catalog Migration Template
nodes.rationale: Catalog establishes the concrete vertical-slice conventions other domain migrations should reproduce while eliminating host-runtime coupling.

nodes.label: Hosting Commerce and Service-Lifecycle Core
nodes.rationale: Panel1 should be an API-first, reliable and extensible operating layer for hosting providers rather than a complete WHMCS clone.

nodes.label: BullMQ-backed Event Bus
nodes.rationale: Durable outbox support, retries, backoff, configurable concurrency, and an in-memory fallback make event delivery production-capable.

nodes.label: Hono-only HTTP Server
nodes.rationale: Express is planned to be removed after Hono becomes the sole HTTP server.

nodes.label: Host Infrastructure Services
nodes.rationale: Email, encryption, retry/resilience, logging, and errors are supplied through BootOptions.hostInfra and module context rather than core singletons.

nodes.label: BullMQ-backed Job Scheduler
nodes.rationale: Jobs support BullMQ repeatables with node-cron fallback, retry/backoff/timeout settings, manual runs, and execution metrics.

nodes.label: Legacy Event and Job Bridge
nodes.rationale: The bridge retires duplicate event buses and schedulers by routing retained legacy workers and crons through the core runtime.

nodes.label: Module Loader
nodes.rationale: Boot is dependency-ordered, isolates failed modules, and shuts down jobs, events, teardowns, then the database.

nodes.label: Module Manifest Endpoint
nodes.rationale: The active module manifest exposes UI declarations so frontend navigation and routes can be built dynamically.

nodes.label: orval-generated REST Client
nodes.rationale: Aggregated OpenAPI should generate React Query hooks and replace tRPC dependencies.

nodes.label: @panel1/core
nodes.rationale: Core centralizes reusable infrastructure and uses factories rather than global singletons.
